products.name: Hour One
products.note: AI avatar video; virtual presenters; enterprise video; likeness consent; Israeli vendor

reading.body:
Hour One is an Israeli vendor of AI avatar video, selling virtual presenters and enterprise video with likeness consent built into the product.

The company sits in video generation, not in the compute or power layer. Its product is a model-driven service, so its real cost structure runs through inference on rented accelerators rather than through anything it owns. That makes it a buyer of compute, not a builder of it, and it means the grid constraint reaches it as a price on its suppliers rather than as a limit on its own sites.

The data covers a name, a website, a category, and a one-line product note. It does not give funding, headcount, customers, model architecture, or any figure for training or inference volume. Nothing here supports a claim about how much compute Hour One consumes or where that compute sits.

The likeness consent note is the one detail with regulatory weight, and the data does not say which jurisdictions it covers or how consent is enforced. Read the entry as a pointer to a vendor in a crowded category, not as evidence about its scale or its draw on the grid.
